newsitem.title: spain: Basque nationalists released after questioning.
newsitem.headline: Basque nationalists released after questioning.

text.p: Police released two leaders of the political arm of Basque separatist movement ETA on Wednesday after questioning them about an illegal demonstration, the Basque interior ministry said.

Rufi Etxeberria and Jon Idigoras had been arrested after ignoring two court summons to testify about a radical nationalist Herri Batasuna (Popular Unity) protest timed to clash with a demonstration in favour of local police, following the killing of two police officers by a separatist.
The Basque interior ministry had expressly banned the nationalist march on December 14.
Members of Herri Batasuna (HB) routinely disregard court instructions as part of their refusal to "recognise the legitimacy of the Spanish state".
Idigoras, the group's main spokesman, said they had refused to answer any of the Basque high court's questions.
"We are not prepared to voluntarily attend a court hearing, nor to testify, nor answer questions when our fundamental rights are at stake, as is the case here," he said.
The high court also ordered the arrest of another member of HB's executive committee, Jose Maria Olarra, but he could not be found and his summons had been postponed.

Idigoras was held in jail in February on charges of collaborating with an armed group after showing a banned election campaign video featuring armed and hooded members of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
ETA has killed some 800 people since 1968 in its campaign for an independent Basque state.
